newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-JETS NAME BELICHICK COACH, PARCELLS TO FOLLOW.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-JETS NAME BELICHICK COACH, PARCELLS TO FOLLOW.

text.p: The New York Jets announced Tuesday that Bill Belichick would be their head coach for next season with Super Bowl coach Bill Parcells waiting in the wings to take over for the 1998 season.

The Jets said Parcells, prohibited from coaching in the NFL next season without permission from the New England Patriots, had been hired as a consultant and would take over as head coach and chief of football operations on February 1, 1998.
But the Parcells saga was far from over with the Jets' surprise announcement.
The Patriots issued a statement blasting the arrangement as "a transparent farce" and said they intend to ask NFL commissioner Paul Tagliabue to intervene.

"This 'so-called' consulting agreement is a transparent farce and the latest in a series of actions by the New York Jets and Bill Parcells, which further demonstrates it has been their intention all along to have Bill become head coach of the Jets for the 1997 season," the Patriots' statement said.

"We will immediately ask Commissioner Tagliabue to review this agreement between the Jets and Bill Parcells to determine if there has been a violation of Parcells' agreement with the Patriots and the commissioner's ruling last week, which prevents him from serving in this de facto coaching position for another NFL team in 1997," the Patriots said.
The NFL issued a statement earlier Tuesday, saying Tagliabue would review the deal between the Jets and Parcells if called upon to do so, "including holding a hearing if necessary."
Tagliabue ruled last week that Parcells could not serve as a head coach in the NFL in 1997 without the Patriots' permission, due to contractual obligations to New England.
"The Jets were neither denied nor given permission to make a consulting agreement with Parcells for 1997," the NFL statement said.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft had demanded the top overall pick in the upcoming draft be included as compensation for the rights to Parcells this year. The Jets said they would not give up the top draft pick.

It was expected, however, that the Jets would negotiate some form of compensation package for New England to bring Parcells to the sidelines in time for next season, until Tuesday's surprise announcement.
Parcells defended the consulting arrangement in a telephone hook-up to the news conference at Jets' headquarters in Hempstead, New York.

"(The commissioner's ruling) addressed the fact that I could not be a head coach or (serve) in a comparable position," Parcells said. "I don't think being a consultant with the limited role and limited hours is a comparable position."
Parcells, perhaps accurately predicting the Patriots' reaction, insisted his role next season with the Jets would be strictly "in an advisory capacity."
"I am very, very grateful to the Jets and extremely happy with this opportunity," Parcells said.
"I want to tell the Jet fans that we won't rest until we get the job done," he promised the long-suffering Jets faithful, who have not seen their team win a championship since 1969.
"Bill (Belichick) and I will work in concert," he said.

Belichick, a former head coach of the Cleveland Browns, was assistant head coach to Parcells last season with the AFC champion Patriots, 35-21 losers to the Green Bay Packers in the Super Bowl. He was also as an assistant to Parcells during two Super Bowl championship seasons with the New York Giants.
Jets president Steve Gutman made it clear that Belichick was an interim choice until Parcells became available.

"The arrangement we have made with Bill Belichick today is effective now," Gutman said. "He has worked with Bill Parcells for many years. When Bill Parcells takes over as coach, Bill Belichick will become the assistant head coach."
Belichick said he was not worried he might be treated by players as a lame duck because of the unusual arrangement.
"I believe in this programme. I believe the players will have to buy into this programme. Bill (Parcells) and I have won together before and we will win again now," Belichick said.

Kraft on Monday hired San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Pete Carroll to succeed Parcells as Patriots head coach. Ironically, Carroll joined the 49ers after being fired as Jets head coach two seasons ago.
Belichick, 44, replaces Rich Kotite, who resigned after guiding the Jets to a dismal 1-15 mark this past season and a 4-28 record over the past two seasons.
